subject: ClearBridge throughput gap — emergency authorization and immediate mitigation
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@clearbridge.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@clearbridge.com
Date: 2027-09-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production throughput shortfall / 5xx spike (ClearBridge reserved pool)

Aditya —

We're seeing a sustained drop in effective reserved throughput on our Redwood Dedicated pool this morning. Our contract shows 5,000 reserved QPS for inference across our three ingestion endpoints; over the last 12 hours our telemetry shows sustained throughput closer to ~1.6K, and a spike of 5xx errors (auth failures + model OOMs) starting ~03:00 UTC. Latency tail is also elevated (p95 up from 120ms to ~520ms). This is customer-impacting — payment authorizations are timing out and our retry logic is amplifying load.

Attached: clearbridge_error_log_20270916.csv (sample of 5xx traces)

We need immediate clarity on:
- Why reduced effective throughput when committed capacity exists
- Whether this is noisy-neighbor or scheduler misallocation
- Temporary mitigations to get us back to SLA

Please escalate — we will route this to our ops/execs if you need formal exec involvement. We need a timeline for remediation (minutes -> hours).

Thanks,
Sam

Sam — thanks for the alert and the sample logs. We're on it. Quick summary of next steps from our side (initial triage):

1) Engineering triage (Irene) to run a headroom and allocation check across the dedicated pool clusters serving your reservation.
2) Ops (Marissa) to inspect scheduler decisions (spillover, preemption) and look for noisy tenants.
3) Short-term mitigation: if we confirm hot K/V cache pressure or model OOMs, we can temporarily route critical routes to a pinned fallback variant (smaller quantized model) to restore throughput while we debug.
4) If capacity is exhausted cluster-wide, I'll request emergency burst allocation (authorization required from execs) and provide an ETA.

Can you confirm: are all three endpoints experiencing the same symptoms? Any recent traffic pattern changes on your side (batching, sudden prefix expansion)? Also please share your contractual committed QPS window (I have HS-47291 on file).

I'll keep this as a priority. Marissa / Irene — please share an initial triage note within 30 minutes and any required asks for burst / credits.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Customer Success (Escalations), Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@clearbridge.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-16T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production throughput shortfall / 5xx spike (ClearBridge reserved pool)

Sam / Aditya — initial findings from the ops side (rolled up):

• Observed: Dedicated cluster serving ClearBridge reservation (cluster-id CL-7a) shows sustained GPU utilization at 96% across the shard group, and queue depth growth consistent with headroom exhaustion.
• Error breakdown: ~62% of 5xx are internal inference OOMs from the xL model variant when sequence lengths exceed 1.2k tokens; ~28% are NATS auth timeouts (transient control-plane latencies); remainder are per-request rate-limits being hit due to token spikes.
• Root suspects: (a) sustained high-concurrency synthetic workload from an adjacent reserved tenant (noisy neighbor) causing runtime kernel contention; (b) a recent metric-slope change in ClearBridge traffic — your telemetry shows a 3x spike in inferred token-per-request in the early morning window which increases KV cache pressure.

Immediate mitigations we propose (order of execution):
1) Canary route 10% of traffic to quantized medium model variant (latency tradeoff minimal) — expected to reduce OOMs and increase throughput.
2) Enable aggressive prefix caching for top-50 prefixes seen in your traffic to reduce compute for repeated prompts (we can push this in ~30 min).
3) Request emergency burst authorization for +30% GPU capacity (nonce request to execs) while we isolate noisy tenant. This avoids throttling your committed QPS while we triage.

Operational ask for ClearBridge: please confirm whether you can accept the temporary model variant for the next 4 hours and whether any routes must remain on the current variant (regulatory reasons). If you approve, we'll schedule the 10% canary immediately and expand to 100% in a controlled ramp if metrics are stable.

Attachments: sample traces (clearbridge_error_log_20270916.csv) included.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production throughput shortfall / 5xx spike (ClearBridge reserved pool) — emergency approval

Team — thanks for the quick triage. Approve the following emergency actions for ClearBridge (revenue-impacting customer):

1) Grant a temporary +30% burst on dedicated capacity for CL-7a for 48 hours. Ops: coordinate with provisioning to allocate immediately and validate routes (Marissa).
2) Approve route canary to quantized medium model for the suggested critical endpoints; monitor p95/p99 and error rates for 1 hour after each 10% ramp.
3) Provide a one-time customer credit (pro-rata) for any request failures during this event — finance will calculate after postmortem. Aditya: coordinate the messaging and customer-facing timeline.

I want a short internal postmortem (48h) and a contract-level remediation path if we confirm reserved capacity misallocation across the cluster. CCing Legal for potential MSA redlines and Deduct/Makewhole language.

Aditya — please confirm once burst is live and send an external note to ClearBridge with the plan and expected timeline.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
